title: Inject Config via ConfigMap
description: Create a ConfigMap and use it both as environment variables and a volume mount.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal Create a ConfigMap `web-config` with two keys: `APP_PORT=8080` and a file `index.html` with content `

Hello from ConfigMap

`. Then deploy an nginx Pod that: - Sets the environment variable `NGINX_PORT` from `APP_PORT`. - Mounts the `index.html` file into `/usr/share/nginx/html/index.html`. ### Steps 1. Create the ConfigMap using a YAML file `web-config.yaml` (key: `index.html`, value as the HTML). Include `APP_PORT` as a second key. 2. Apply the ConfigMap: `kubectl apply -f web-config.yaml`. 3. Create a Pod YAML `nginx-config-pod.yaml`: - image: nginx:1.25 - env: `NGINX_PORT` from configmap key `APP_PORT` - volume from `web-config` with `items` to mount only `index.html` - mount the volume at `/usr/share/nginx/html` 4. Apply the Pod: `kubectl apply -f nginx-config-pod.yaml`. 5. Forward the port: `kubectl port-forward pod/nginx-config-pod 8080:80`. 6. Access `http://localhost:8080` – see the custom HTML. 7. Check the environment variable: `kubectl exec nginx-config-pod -- env | grep NGINX_PORT`. 8. Clean up: delete Pod and ConfigMap.
hints: Use `items` in the volume definition to select only the `index.html` key, mapping `key: index.html` and `path: index.html`.
If port forwarding fails, ensure the Pod is Running and port 80 is correct.
expectedOutput: The nginx home page shows 'Hello from ConfigMap' and the env var `NGINX_PORT` is 8080.
solutionCode:
# web-config.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: web-config data: APP_PORT: "8080" index.html: |

Hello from ConfigMap

# nginx-config-pod.yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: nginx-config-pod spec: containers: - name: nginx image: nginx:1.25 env: - name: NGINX_PORT valueFrom: configMapKeyRef: name: web-config key: APP_PORT volumeMounts: - name: html-volume mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html volumes: - name: html-volume configMap: name: web-config items: - key: index.html path: index.html
